methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.seoDescription: The scientific foundations behind Zoned's 6-zone training system. Based on established sports science research.
methodology.heading: The science behind Zoned
methodology.intro: Every Zoned workout rests on decades of sports science research.
methodology.ourApproachText1: All workouts in Zoned are based on established sports science. The intensity zones are not arbitrary: they correspond to real physiological thresholds that can be measured in a lab or estimated from field tests.
methodology.ourApproachText2: Our 6-zone model is derived from key physiological markers: the first ventilatory threshold (VT1), the second ventilatory threshold (VT2, also called the lactate turn point), and maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max). These thresholds define distinct metabolic states that require specific training stimuli.
methodology.ourApproachDisclaimer: Important: The percentage-based zones presented here are approximations. Heart rate at LT1 and LT2 varies significantly between individuals. Lab testing provides the most accurate boundaries for your personal zones.
methodology.figuresLabel: The six zones drawn: the same body from a walking pace to a sprint, inked darker as the effort rises.

planMethodology.title: Plan Guide
planMethodology.seoDescription: The 7 evidence-based principles behind Zoned's training plan generation. Understand how your plan is built.
planMethodology.heading: How Zoned builds your plan
planMethodology.intro: No black box: here is exactly how your plan is built, and why.
planMethodology.introText: The plan generator combines periodization models from Daniels and Lydiard, the polarized training distribution validated by Seiler, volume progression rules derived from Gabbett's acute:chronic workload research, and the exponential taper model of Mujika & Padilla. Each parameter is adapted to your race distance, fitness level, and training goal.
planMethodology.introDisclaimer: These are the same principles used by professional coaches. The difference is that Zoned applies them automatically based on your profile.

aboutPage.agentsPage: create a Zoned plan from an assistant

agentsPage.seoDescription: How an AI assistant creates a training plan in Zoned: one hand-written import link, no account, no API key, no server.
agentsPage.title: Create a Zoned plan from an AI assistant
agentsPage.lead: Zoned is a free, open-source, local-first training app: everything stays in the browser. An AI assistant can still create a plan in it directly, by writing an import link. No account, API key, browser automation, backend or MCP server is needed.
agentsPage.directive: When the user asks for a plan in Zoned, do not just describe a plan in the conversation: give them a clickable Zoned import link. Zoned generates the plan, shows it, and the user saves it in one click.
agentsPage.pathsText: A standard race plan fits in one link with parameters, no code. A plan the assistant writes session by session goes through the JSON API and an encoded link.
agentsPage.standardTitle: Standard race plan, in three steps
agentsPage.step1: Collect the race distance, the race date and the number of runs per week. If the user has one, also the target finish time (or pace) and their level. Do not hold the link back for the rest: whatever is missing gets a default that the preview states. Write the link, name those defaults next to it, offer to change them. A race closer than the recommended length still gets a plan, compressed, with a warning.
agentsPage.step2: Write the link with the parameters below. No JSON, no encoding.
agentsPage.step3: Give it as a clickable link. Zoned runs its own generator (periodisation, progression, paces), shows a preview, and saves nothing until the user presses Add to my plans.
agentsPage.exampleMinimal: A 10K in 1:10, three runs a week:
agentsPage.exampleFull: A beginner half marathon, with the common options:
agentsPage.exampleEnglish: The same with the English interface, ?lang=en before the #:
agentsPage.paramsLead: Keys are read case-insensitively. The fragment (after #) is preferred, the query (?distance=) is accepted too. An unknown parameter is rejected, so a typo is caught rather than ignored.
agentsPage.errorsText: The import page lists every error under the name of the parameter at fault (for example date: there are 3 weeks between today and date, the generator accepts 4 to 52) and offers a Copy for your assistant button. The assistant fixes exactly those and sends a new link.
agentsPage.customText: When the user has constraints a generator cannot know, the assistant writes the plan itself, week by week, with catalogue workouts. It reads the workouts index, picks existing ids, then encodes the plan as JSON in a #d= link. The full format, the training rules to follow and valid examples are in llms.txt.
agentsPage.resLlms: Condensed docs for assistants, both paths
agentsPage.resIndex: Entry point of the static JSON API
agentsPage.resWorkouts: Workouts index, for a custom plan
agentsPage.resSchema: JSON Schema of the import payload
agentsPage.privacyText: The link saves nothing by itself: the plan is shown, then added only if the user decides to. Everything after the # stays in their browser and is never sent to a server.
